records.title: The Model T reaches its first customer
records.claim: Ford's Model T was shipped to its first customer on October 1, 1908, helping make car travel more affordable for many families.

records.title: Peanuts appears in newspapers
records.claim: Charles Schulz's Peanuts comic strip first appeared on October 2, 1950.

records.title: Transistor inventors receive a patent
records.claim: The inventors of the transistor received a patent on October 3, 1950, helping make modern electronics possible.

records.title: Sputnik beeps from space
records.claim: Sputnik 1 launched on October 4, 1957, becoming the first artificial satellite in Earth orbit.

records.title: World Teachers' Day begins
records.claim: UNESCO says World Teachers' Day has been celebrated every October 5 since 1994.

records.title: Moulin Rouge opens
records.claim: The Moulin Rouge opened in Paris on October 6, 1889.

records.title: The barcode patent is granted
records.claim: Norman Woodland and Bernard Silver received a patent for a barcode design on October 7, 1952, an early step toward faster store checkouts.

records.eventYearNote: World Octopus Day is a recurring calendar observance rather than a single historical event.
records.title: Octopus Day
records.claim: World Octopus Day celebrates an animal with eight arms and remarkable problem-solving skills.

records.title: The Universal Postal Union is founded
records.claim: The Universal Postal Union was founded on October 9, 1874, and that anniversary is remembered as World Post Day.

records.title: World Mental Health Day
records.claim: World Mental Health Day has been observed on October 10 since 1992.

records.eventYearNote: International Day of the Girl is an annual observance established by the United Nations in 2011.
records.title: The International Day of the Girl
records.claim: October 11 is a day that highlights girls' rights and opportunities to learn and grow.

records.title: Many astronauts share one spacecraft
records.claim: Voskhod 1 launched on October 12, 1964, carrying the first crew of more than one person without spacesuits.

records.title: Disaster risk gets its own day
records.claim: The United Nations designated October 13 as the International Day for Disaster Risk Reduction in 1999.

records.title: An airplane breaks the sound barrier
records.claim: Chuck Yeager flew faster than sound on October 14, 1947, in the Bell X-1 aircraft.

records.title: Clean hands get a special day
records.claim: The first Global Handwashing Day was held on October 15, 2008, to teach how soap and water help prevent illness.

records.title: Disney Brothers Cartoon Studio begins
records.claim: Walt and Roy Disney signed a contract on October 16, 1923, beginning their cartoon studio story.

records.eventYearNote: International Day for the Eradication of Poverty is an annual observance held every October 17.
records.title: Small actions can help communities
records.claim: October 17 is a day for learning how communities can work together to reduce poverty.

records.title: The BBC begins broadcasting
records.claim: The British Broadcasting Company began broadcasting on October 18, 1922.

records.eventYearNote: International Repair Day is a recurring observance whose date is set by its organizers.
records.title: Repair instead of replace
records.claim: Repair events encourage people to fix useful objects rather than throw them away.

records.title: The first World Statistics Day
records.claim: The first World Statistics Day was celebrated worldwide on October 20, 2010, highlighting how reliable data help people understand progress and challenges.

records.title: Edison tests a long-lasting lamp
records.claim: Thomas Edison demonstrated a practical incandescent lamp that stayed lit for many hours in October 1879.

records.title: A parachute opens over Paris
records.claim: André-Jacques Garnerin made the first recorded parachute jump from a balloon on October 22, 1797.

records.title: Pelé is born
records.claim: Brazilian football player Pelé was born on October 23, 1940.

records.title: Annie Taylor rides over Niagara Falls
records.claim: Teacher Annie Edson Taylor survived going over Niagara Falls in a barrel on October 24, 1901, attempting a daring challenge.

records.title: Picasso is born
records.claim: Artist Pablo Picasso was born on October 25, 1881, in Málaga, Spain.

records.title: The Erie Canal opens
records.claim: The Erie Canal opened on October 26, 1825, linking Lake Erie with the Hudson River and making a major new route for travel and trade.

records.title: New York's subway opens
records.claim: New York City's first subway line opened on October 27, 1904.

records.title: The Statue of Liberty is dedicated
records.claim: The Statue of Liberty was dedicated in New York Harbor on October 28, 1886.

records.title: The first ARPANET message begins with “LO”
records.claim: On October 29, 1969, a UCLA team sent the first ARPANET host-to-host message toward the Stanford Research Institute; the system stopped after “LO.”

records.title: A radio drama sounds like news
records.claim: Orson Welles's radio adaptation of The War of the Worlds aired on October 30, 1938, and some listeners mistook parts for news.

records.eventYearNote: Halloween is a recurring cultural observance with roots in older seasonal traditions, not one single dated event.
records.title: Halloween's older seasonal roots
records.claim: Halloween is connected with older autumn traditions about the changing season and remembering the dead.
